newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania coalminers leader detained over 1991 riots.
newsitem.headline: Romania coalminers leader detained over 1991 riots.

text.p: Romanian police has detained vigilante miners' leader Miron Cosma in connection with his role in leading bloody coalminer riots which toppled the first post-communist government in 1991, prosecutors said on Friday.

Cosma was taken into police custody on a 30-day warrant issued by prosecutors on charges including "undermining state authority" and breaking firearms regulations, the general prosecutor's office told Reuters.
He could face up to 15 years jail, a spokeswoman said, declining to give further details.

Cosma won notoriety when he led thousands of coalminers on a three-day rampage to Bucharest in 1991, during which government offices were torched and three people were killed during clashes with police.
Former reformist Prime Minister Petre Roman was forced to quit during those riots, which he later blamed on a putsch engineered by communists around ex-president Ion Iliescu.
A date for a trial has yet to be set. Cosma's lawyers could not immediately be reached.

Cosma ran for office in his Jiu Valley fiefdom but his bid for a parliament seat was thwarted in general and presidential elections last November, when Iliescu's leftwingers were thrown out of office for the first time in seven years.

Romania's new centrist ruling coalition has pledged to bring to justice those responsible for several waves of political violence, in which Cosma's miners ransacked opposition party offices and beat up anti-government protesters in the early post-communist years.
